subject.title: fix(message): ignore populated location on text sends

question: Should mixed `location` plus text/media/presentation requests remain an explicit error, or should OpenClaw adopt a documented precedence rule that silently drops location data?
rationale: Current public documentation defines location as a standalone send mode, while this PR changes that API behavior globally and can discard a user-requested location; the intended compatibility policy cannot be inferred safely from the patch.

options.title: Keep fail-fast validation
options.body: Retain the current rejection and fix any tool-call generator that emits optional location defaults when it does not intend a location send.

options.title: Adopt explicit precedence
options.body: Accept mixed payloads only with a documented and tested precedence rule that explains when location data is discarded.

options.title: Add an explicit generator marker
options.body: Normalize known generated-default location fields before send validation without changing the public mixed-payload contract for ordinary callers.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-fast validation
recommendation.body: Retain the current rejection and fix any tool-call generator that emits optional location defaults when it does not intend a location send.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing lead for an outbound API and product-contract decision.
